body:
Crypto markets endured another bruising session Friday as the broader selloff accelerated into the weekend, with total market cap sliding 2.66% to $2.69T on elevated $85.5B volume. Fear & Greed dropped to 31 from yesterday's 43, confirming the shift in sentiment as leveraged positions continued unwinding. The selling was broad-based but measured, lacking the panic characteristics of previous major corrections. BTC dominance held steady at 58.3% while ETH dominance compressed to 9.8%, suggesting investors are rotating toward perceived safety rather than fleeing crypto entirely.

Bitcoin tested key support at $78,431, down 2.71% on the day with $34.22B in volume driving the decline. The move broke below the critical $80,000 psychological level that had provided support over recent weeks, though buyers emerged near $78,000 to prevent further deterioration. Next major support sits at $75,500, while any recovery needs to reclaim $82,000 to signal the correction has run its course. The 7-day decline of 2.23% remains manageable, but momentum has clearly shifted bearish after weeks of consolidation.

Ethereum underperformed with a 2.74% drop to $2,194, extending the weekly decline to 5.19% as the ETH/BTC ratio continues deteriorating. Solana led major alt losses with a 4.24% slide to $87.50, while traditional large caps like ADA and DOT shed 4.47% and 5.17% respectively. Chainlink's 5.10% decline reflects broader DeFi weakness. Surprisingly, Uniswap bucked the trend with a late-day 0.96% hourly surge, though still closed down 4.16%. The altcoin rout suggests risk-off positioning as traders reduce exposure ahead of the weekend.

The selloff appears driven by profit-taking rather than fundamental deterioration, with Bhutan disputing reports of $1B in bitcoin sales that had spooked markets earlier. US regulatory clarity continues improving with House lawmakers pushing Trump to fill CFTC vacancies and the CLARITY Act generating optimism. However, traditional markets remain under pressure from persistent inflation concerns and geopolitical tensions, creating headwinds for risk assets. The Fear & Greed reading of 31 suggests capitulation may be approaching, historically a positive contrarian signal.

Key catalysts next week include SpaceX's June 11 IPO announcement and potential CFTC nominations from the Trump administration. Immediate support at $78,000 for BTC and $2,150 for ETH will determine if this correction deepens or finds a floor. Any break below these levels could trigger cascading liquidations, while a bounce back above $80,000 and $2,250 respectively would signal the dip-buying opportunity many have been waiting for. Watch funding rates and open interest for signs that leverage has been sufficiently flushed from the system.
